title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete data samples, where traditional deletion or imputation-based approaches lose information or introduce bias. It proposes the proximity kernel, which combines equal-frequency binning, proximity (Voronoi) assignment, one-hot encoding, and a three-level cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding for missing features. Experiments on 12 UCI incomplete datasets show the proposed method achieves the highest average NMI of 0.4245, best or second-best NMI on 10 of 12 datasets, and linear time complexity in the number of samples.

approach: Reimplement the proximity kernel from the paper for the target claim C1 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset. For each feature, equal-frequency binning uses evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values only, then each observed value is assigned to its nearest bin center and encoded as a one-hot vector. Missing feature encodings are filled by a three-level cascading fallback (intersection matching, union matching, global prior) using kernel mean embedding over matching samples. The resulting representation Z is clustered with sklearn KMeans using the ground-truth number of clusters, NMI is averaged over 10 random seeds, and nbins is searched over {2,3,4,6,8} by mean NMI. Finally, reproduce.py writes results/metrics.json comparing the selected NMI to the target 0.2289 within ±0.02.
steps: Setup: confirm numpy, pandas, scikit-learn are installed. No extra packages are required because pandas can read the UCI URL directly. Set all random seeds via the seed lists in config.

Implement src/data.py: read https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data with pandas.read_csv(header=None, na_values=['?', '']); X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).values; y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).values - 1; assert X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), len(np.unique(y)) == 2; return X, y, K=2.

Implement src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins(X, nbins): for each feature j, obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]; if len(obs) == 0, centers = None and prior = uniform 1/nbins; else centers = np.percentile(obs, 100*np.arange(1, nbins+1)/(nbins+1), method='linear'); store centers and global prior frequencies.

Implement proximity_kernel.py assign_bins(X, centers): for each observed value, k = np.argmin(np.abs(x - centers)); tie breaks to lowest index; store integer bin assignments B (n, d) with -1 for missing entries.
Implement proximity_kernel.py encode_observed(B, nbins): build H_obs (n, d, nbins) with H_obs[i, j, B[i, j]] = 1 for observed entries, zeros for missing entries.

Implement proximity_kernel.py compute_fallback_encodings(X, B, H_obs, centers, nbins): for each missing entry (i, j), let O_i = observed features of i and B_i = B[i, O_i]. Level 1: S1 = {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l] for all l in O_i}; S1_j = {m in S1 : X[m, j] observed}; if S1_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S1_j). Level 2: if S1_j empty, S2 = union_{l in O_i} {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l]}; S2_j = {m in S2 : X[m, j] observed}; if S2_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S2_j). Level 3: if S2_j empty, h = global prior for feature j (bin frequencies among observed values, or uniform 1/nbins if feature entirely missing). Store H[i, j] = h and record level counts.

Implement proximity_kernel.py build_representation(X, nbins): call fit_bins, assign_bins, encode_observed, compute_fallback_encodings; concatenate H[i, j] across j to get Z (n, d*nbins); return Z and diagnostics including missing entry count and level 1/2/3 counts.
Implement proximity_kernel.py proximity_kernel(Z): return K = Z @ Z.T / d where d = 19; use only for symmetry and bounds checks.

Implement src/cluster.py evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds): for each seed, run KMeans(n_clusters=K, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit(Z); labels = kmeans.labels_; nmi = normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels); return mean, std, per-seed list.

Implement src/cluster.py search_nbins(X, y, K, nbins_grid, seeds): for each nbins in nbins_grid, call build_representation, evaluate_nbins, and record mean/std/per-seed; select best nbins as the one with highest mean NMI; return best_nbins, best_mean, all_results.

Implement reproduce.py: parse optional --smoke flag. If smoke, load data, subset first 20 rows, run build_representation with nbins=2, assert Z.shape == (20, 38), assert no NaN/inf, assert each observed-feature one-hot sums to 1 and each missing-feature fallback vector sums to 1, compute K and assert symmetry and diagonal <= 1, run one KMeans with seed 0, print NMI and diagnostics. Otherwise run search_nbins on full Hepatitis with nbins_grid and seeds.
Run smoke test: python reproduce.py --smoke. Verify output shows correct shapes, no NaNs, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, and a valid NMI in [0, 1].

Run intermediate checks before full run: print X shape (155, 19), y shape (155,), class counts, total missing entries and per-feature missing counts; verify bin centers are strictly increasing for features with observed values; verify B indices are in [0, nbins-1]; verify H row sums per feature are 1 for all samples; print fallback level counts (level 3 should be rare, <5% of missing entries); verify K is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, K_ij in [0, 1]; run a sanity baseline KMeans on median-imputed raw features and record its NMI for reference.
Run full reproduction: python reproduce.py. This runs 5 nbins values × 10 seeds = 50 KMeans runs on 155 samples; each run is seconds or less.

Inspect results/metrics.json: check the C1 value, best_nbins, per-nbins means, and per-seed NMI spread. Compare |value - 0.2289| <= 0.02. If outside tolerance, run sensitivity variants: (a) percentile centers at 100*(k-0.5)/nbins; (b) percentile centers at 100*k/nbins; (c) kernel K-means assigning each point to the cluster maximizing average K to cluster members. Record each variant's value and choose the most faithful documented variant; otherwise keep the primary result.
Finalize results/metrics.json with the chosen C1 value, target 0.2289, tolerance 0.02, pass/fail boolean, best nbins, per-nbins and per-seed results, diagnostics, runtime, and environment metadata.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --smoke: loads Hepatitis, subsets first 20 rows, builds Z with nbins=2, checks Z shape == (20, 38), no NaN/inf, each feature encoding sums to 1 per sample, kernel K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric with diagonal <= 1, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, runs KMeans(n_clusters=2, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=0), and prints an NMI in [0, 1].
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), number of classes == 2.
Class balance: print counts of y == 0 and y == 1 (expected approximately 32/123 for Hepatitis; exact counts are fine).
Missingness: total number of NaN entries and per-feature NaN counts; confirm common UCI missing markers '?' were converted to NaN.
Binning: for each feature with observed values, the nbins bin centers are strictly increasing; for any entirely missing feature, uniform prior is used.
Proximity assignment: all non-missing bin indices B[i, j] are in [0, nbins-1]; missing entries are -1.
One-hot encoding: for every sample and every feature, the encoding vector h_{i,j} sums to 1 (exactly 1 for observed, probabilities summing to 1 for missing).
Fallback diagnostics: count missing entries resolved by level 1, level 2, and level 3; level 3 should be rare (<5% of missing entries).
Kernel matrix: K = Z @ Z.T / 19 is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, and all entries are in [0, 1].
Sanity baseline: KMeans on raw features with median imputation gives some NMI; record it to ensure the proximity kernel result is not identical to a trivial imputation baseline.
Parameter count: Z has shape (155, 19*nbins); for nbins in {2,3,4,6,8} this is 38, 57, 76, 114, 152 features.
budget_plan: Total ~15-20 min for target C1: setup and dependency check 2 min, data download and parsing 1 min, implementation of data/proximity_kernel/cluster 5 min, smoke test 1 min, intermediate checks and diagnostics 3 min, full 5 nbins × 10 seeds KMeans/NMI run on 155 samples 5 min, write and verify results/metrics.json 2 min. """Proximity kernel representation for incomplete data (paper Sections 4.1-4.3).

Pipeline (all steps follow the paper's equations):
  1. Equal-frequency bin centers from observed values only  -- Eq. (4):
         c_{j,k} = percentile(X_obs,j, (k-1)*100/(nbins-1)),  k = 1..nbins
     so the first/last centers are the min/max of the observed values.
  2. Proximity assignment of each observed value to its nearest center -- Eq. (5).
  3. One-hot encoding of observed features, concatenated over features -- Eqs. (6)-(7).
  4. Three-level cascading fallback for missing features -- Eqs. (8)-(14):
       level 1: intersection matching S1(i) (Eq. 8-9), kernel mean embedding (Eq. 10)
       level 2: union matching S2(i) (Eq. 11), KME (Eq. 12)
       level 3: global prior over bins (Eq. 13-14)
  5. Representation z_i in R^{d*nbins}; proximity kernel K = (1/d) Z Z^T -- Eq. (15).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np


def bin_center_percentiles(nbins: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Percentile levels for Eq. (4): (k-1)*100/(nbins-1), k = 1..nbins."""
    if nbins < 2:
        raise ValueError("nbins must be >= 2 (Eq. 4 divides by nbins-1)")
    k = np.arange(1, nbins + 1, dtype=float)
    return (k - 1) * 100.0 / (nbins - 1)


def nearest_center_idx(values: np.ndarray, centers: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Eq. (5): index of nearest center; ties resolved to the lowest index."""
    dist = np.abs(np.asarray(values, dtype=float)[:, None] - centers[None, :])
    return np.argmin(dist, axis=1)


def fit_bins(X: np.ndarray, nbins: int):
    """Return (centers [d, nbins], prior [d, nbins]) from observed values only.

    prior[j] is the global bin distribution of feature j (Eq. 13), used by the
    level-3 fallback; for an entirely-missing feature it is uniform (A7).
    """
    n, d = X.shape
    levels = bin_center_percentiles(nbins)
    centers = np.full((d, nbins), np.nan)
    prior = np.full((d, nbins), 1.0 / nbins)
    for j in range(d):
        col = X[:, j]
        obs = col[~np.isnan(col)]
        if obs.size == 0:
            continue  # entirely missing feature: uniform prior, centers unused
        centers[j] = np.percentile(obs, levels, method="linear")  # A2
        b = nearest_center_idx(obs, centers[j])
        prior[j] = np.bincount(b, minlength=nbins) / float(obs.size)
    return centers, prior


def assign_bins(X: np.ndarray, centers: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """B[i,j] in {0..nbins-1} for observed entries, -1 for missing (Eq. 5)."""
    n, d = X.shape
    nbins = centers.shape[1]
    B = np.full((n, d), -1, dtype=int)
    for j in range(d):
        col = X[:, j]
        mask = ~np.isnan(col)
        if mask.any():
            B[mask, j] = nearest_center_idx(col[mask], centers[j])
    assert B[B >= 0].max() < nbins and B[B >= 0].min() >= 0
    return B

    """Eqs. (6)-(7): one-hot encodings for observed entries, zeros elsewhere."""
    n, d = B.shape
    H = np.zeros((n, d, nbins), dtype=float)
    obs = B >= 0
    rows, cols = np.nonzero(obs)
    H[rows, cols, B[rows, cols]] = 1.0
    return H

    """Three-level cascading fallback (Eqs. (8)-(14)) for all missing entries.

    Matching sets follow the paper:
      C_{i,j} = {m != i : b_{m,j} = b_{i,j}}   (m must have feature j observed)
      S1(i)   = intersection over observed features (Eq. 9)
      S2(i)   = union over observed features       (Eq. 11)

"""K-means clustering on the proximity-kernel representation + NMI evaluation.

Protocol (paper Section 5.1, R10-R12):
  - K-means with n_clusters = ground-truth number of classes (Eq. 19 clusters
    in representation space, i.e. K-means on z_i).
  - each experiment repeated 10 times, average NMI reported.
  - nbins searched over {2, 3, 4, 6, 8}, selecting the best mean NMI per dataset.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
from sklearn.metrics import normalized_mutual_info_score

from src.proximity_kernel import build_representation

DEFAULT_SEEDS = list(range(10))  # 10 runs (R11)
DEFAULT_N_INIT = 10


def kmeans_nmi(Z, y, k, seed, n_init=DEFAULT_N_INIT):
    km = KMeans(n_clusters=k, init="k-means++", n_init=n_init, random_state=seed)
    labels = km.fit_predict(Z)
    return float(normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels)), labels


def evaluate_representation(Z, y, k, seeds=None, n_init=DEFAULT_N_INIT):
    seeds = DEFAULT_SEEDS if seeds is None else seeds
    per_seed = []
    for s in seeds:
        nmi, _ = kmeans_nmi(Z, y, k, s, n_init=n_init)
        per_seed.append(nmi)
    return {
        "mean": float(np.mean(per_seed)),
        "std": float(np.std(per_seed)),
        "min": float(np.min(per_seed)),
        "max": float(np.max(per_seed)),
        "per_seed": per_seed,
        "seeds": list(seeds),
    }


def search_nbins(X, y, k, nbins_grid, seeds=None, n_init=DEFAULT_N_INIT):
    """Evaluate every nbins setting; select the best mean NMI (assumption A9)."""
    results = []
    for nb in nbins_grid:
        Z, diag = build_representation(X, int(nb))
        ev = evaluate_representation(Z, y, k, seeds=seeds, n_init=n_init)
        results.append({"nbins": int(nb), "Z_shape": list(Z.shape),
                        "diagnostics": diag, **ev})
        print(f"  nbins={nb:>2}: mean NMI={ev['mean']:.4f} "
              f"(std {ev['std']:.4f}, per-seed {['%.3f' % v for v in ev['per_seed']]})")
    best = max(results, key=lambda r: (r["mean"], -r["nbins"]))
    return best["nbins"], best["mean"], results

target.statement: Proximity kernel ('Ours') achieves NMI 0.2289 on the Hepatitis dataset under K-means clustering with the ground-truth number of clusters.
target.dataset: Hepatitis (UCI; 155 samples, 19 features, 2 classes per Table 2)

tolerance.why: Rule 3: NMI is a bounded [0,1] score on the Hepatitis dataset (155 examples, smaller than 2,000) and the paper prints values as fractions, so the band is 0.02 absolute.

audit_summary: The clean rerun (exit 0, 10.8 s) reproduces C1 essentially exactly: measured NMI 0.228909 vs the paper's 0.2289 (diff ~7e-6, far inside the 0.02 tolerance), with identical per-seed values across all 10 K-means seeds. The code is a genuine from-scratch implementation of the paper's pipeline (percentile bin centers from observed values only, nearest-center assignment, per-feature one-hot concatenation, three-level intersection/union/global-prior fallback, K=(1/d)ZZ^T, transductive K-means with ground-truth K, sklearn NMI, nbins grid {2,3,4,6,8}, 10 runs) on the correct data (Hepatitis 155x19, 32/123 classes, 167 NaN entries = 5.67%); no paper value is embedded anywhere (paper_numbers_found_in_code empty) and the reported number is computed from the data. Two caveats must temper the interpretation of the exact match: (i) the implemented Eq. (4) endpoint centers (min/max) do not produce strictly equal-frequency Voronoi bins, and the genuinely equal-frequency 'midpoint' variant scores 0.2134 -- still inside tolerance -- so the 4-decimal agreement is not uniquely forced by the method description; (ii) the level-1/level-2 kernel-mean-embedding estimator uses a renormalization over matching samples with the target feature observed (A8/A14) rather than the literal |S1(i)|/|S2(i)| divisor given in Eqs. (10)/(12), a documented but high-risk deviation that also shifts the number. Nothing was scaled down, no proxy metric or wrong split was used, and the two extra reference baselines (median imputation, kernel-K-means variant) are clearly labelled as the implementer's own; note the z-scored median-imputation reference reaches 0.2583 > 0.2289 on this dataset, which is an internal comparison only and does not affect C1. R13 (linear-time complexity) is unverified, and the reported value is a best-of-grid selection on the same data used for scoring, per the paper's own protocol.

requirement_check.evidence: fit_bins() computes bin centers per feature from observed values only (np.percentile over col[~isnan]) with no imputation; for nbins=2 centers are the observed min/max as the paper's Eq. (4) prescribes. Caveat: with nearest-center (Voronoi) assignment this yields a range-midpoint split, not a strictly equal-count split; the genuinely equal-frequency 'midpoint' variant is reported separately (0.2134).
bin_center_percentiles(nbins,'paper_eq4') = (k-1)*100/(nbins-1), k=1..nbins, computed with method='linear' (assumption A2); run diagnostics confirm centers_nondecreasing=True for all of {2,3,4,6,8}.
nearest_center_idx() takes argmin of |x - c| per feature, ties to lowest index (A3); bin_index_range checks pass ([0,1] ... [0,7]) and missing entries are set to -1.
encode_observed() writes a one-hot vector per observed feature and Z = H.reshape(n, d*nbins); Z shape (155, 38) = (155, 19*2), asserts confirm observed entries are exactly one-hot (max=1, min=0).

compute_fallback_encodings() implements the cascade intersection -> union -> global prior per missing entry; Hepatitis diagnostics: 61 level-1, 106 level-2, 0 level-3, summing to all 167 missing entries.

Level 1 builds S1 as the set of samples matching the bins of all observed features, then sets h_{i,j} = mean one-hot over S1-members with feature j observed (assumptions A8/A14; the literal |S1(i)| divisor is available as kme_norm='literal_eq10' but not reported). Documented refinement of an underspecified equation, not a silent substitution.
Level 2 builds S2 as the union of bin matches over observed features and averages the one-hot encodings of members with feature j observed; used for 106/167 missing entries on Hepatitis.

Level 3 falls back to prior[j], the empirical bin-frequency distribution (uniform for an all-missing feature, A7); implemented but never triggered on Hepatitis (level3_global_prior = 0), so its behaviour is unverified empirically.
proximity_kernel_matrix() computes K = (Z @ Z.T)/d with d = n_features (Eq. 15); checks report symmetric=True, max_diagonal=1.0, min=-0.0, psd min eigenvalue ~ -2.6e-14.

sklearn KMeans(n_clusters=2 = number of ground-truth classes, init='k-means++', n_init=10) on Z, scored with sklearn normalized_mutual_info_score (A4/A5); transductive, full dataset, no held-out split (A10).
10 seeds (0..9) per nbins, mean reported; per_nbins entries list 10 per-seed values (std 0.0 at the selected nbins=2).
grid [2,3,4,6,8] fully evaluated in search_nbins(); best mean NMI selected per dataset (assumption A9), best_nbins=2 with mean 0.2289.

No timing or complexity experiment was run (only 155-sample wall clock, 6.8 s); moreover the fallback constructs an n-length boolean mask per sample in a Python loop, i.e. O(n^2 d), so the paper's linear-in-n claim is neither implemented with bin indexing nor measured.
For observed entries encode_observed() writes exactly one 1 per feature (d ones out of d*nbins), asserted via H[obs_mask].max()==1 and min()==0; d=19, nbins=2 gives 19 ones out of 38 elements.
